title: Flat ringed complete equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal B$ a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings, and $\mathcal J\subset\mathcal O$ an ideal sheaf locally generated by finitely many sections. Let $D(\mathcal O)$ and $D(\mathcal B)$ be the derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Call $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ locally derived $\mathcal J$-complete if, for every $U$ and $f\in\mathcal J(U)$, $R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U[1/f],N|_U)=0$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ is the sheafification of the sectionwise localization on the slice site over $U$. Use the same definition for $\mathcal J\mathcal B$. Assume $\mathcal B$ is flat over $\mathcal O$ [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] and the induced map $\mathcal O/\mathcal J\to\mathcal B/\mathcal J\mathcal B$ is an isomorphism. Then restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] induces an equivalence between the full subcategories of locally derived complete objects in $D(\mathcal B)$ and $D(\mathcal O)$.

source.place: Tag 099I (lemma-restriction-derived-complete-equivalence), with local completeness as in Tag 0999 (definition-derived-complete).

proof.text: Restriction of scalars has the same underlying additive sheaf. Reflect finite limits and finite colimits along the additive-sheaf forgetful functor to prove exactness. The homology comparison for an exact functor proves that derived restriction reflects isomorphisms. The extension-ideal characterization identifies the ideal used by restriction-local-completeness, yielding preservation and reflection of local completeness.

The ideal inclusion is mono by sectionwise subtype injectivity. Apply the extended Cech completion-model theorem, retaining its naturality and its assertion that the unit is an isomorphism on complete objects. Apply flat_ringed_cech_base_change to the augmented model, obtaining KB, epsilonB and a quasi-isomorphism u compatible with augmentations.

Apply ringed_cech_hom_coefficient_action to obtain T, theta:rT -> completion, and beta:id -> Tr. Lift derived restriction to the complete full subcategories. Its inverse is the lift of T: for complete E, the composition of the completion-unit isomorphism with theta inverse identifies E with rT(E); completeness is invariant under isomorphism and reflected by restriction.

For complete M, r(beta_M) composed with theta equals the completion unit at rM. The latter and theta are isomorphisms, so r(beta_M) and then beta_M are isomorphisms by conservativity. This yields the first natural isomorphism of complete functors. Completion-unit naturality and theta naturality give the second. Equivalence.mk assembles them into an equivalence whose functor is literally the lifted derived restriction, so its ambient comparison is the identity natural isomorphism.
